title: Clitic pronouns
about: The short pronouns *με, σε, τον, την, το, μου, σου, του, της…* lean on the verb. They go before every finite verb, including after *θα*, *να*, *δεν*, *μην*, *ας* and before *έχω* in the perfect; they go after an imperative or a gerund. With two clitics the genitive (to whom) comes before the accusative (what): *μου το έδωσε*, *δώσ' μου το*. The person something is given or said to is genitive: *του είπα*, not *τον είπα*.

items.en: I see him every day on the bus.

errs.why: Object clitics go before the verb: *τον βλέπω*, *τη θυμάμαι*.

items.en: I really like Thessaloniki.

errs.why: With *αρέσει* the person who likes is in the genitive: *μου αρέσει*, *σου αρέσει*, *της αρέσουν*.

items.en: I'll do it tomorrow, I promise.

errs.why: *θα* comes first and the clitic sits between *θα* and the verb: *θα το κάνω*.

items.en: I don't know it, ask Maria.

errs.why: After *δεν* the clitic still goes before the verb: *δεν το ξέρω*.

items.en: Pass me the salt, please.

errs.why: With the imperative the clitic follows the verb: *δώσε μου*, *πες μου*, *φέρ' το*.

parts: Σε πήρα τηλέφωνο, αλλά δεν απάντησες.
items.en: I called you, but you didn't answer.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *σε* (accusative) before *πήρα τηλέφωνο*, the usual way to say "call someone".

items.en: I've read it twice.

errs.why: In the perfect the clitic goes before *έχω*: *το έχω διαβάσει*, *την είχα δει*.

items.en: Eleni gave it to me.

errs.why: Two clitics before the verb: genitive first, then accusative: *μου το έδωσε*, *σας τα έστειλα*.

items.en: I want to take it with me.

errs.why: After *να* the clitic goes before the verb: *να το πάρω*.

items.en: Don't tell anyone!

errs.why: *μην* + subjunctive is not an imperative, so the clitic stays in front: *μην το πεις*.

items.en: She told me to wait for him at the stop.

errs.why: *περιμένω* takes a direct object in the accusative: *τον περιμένω*. Only verbs of giving, saying and the like take the genitive.

items.en: I told him not to worry.

errs.why: The person you tell something to is genitive: *του είπα*, *της είπα*, *τους είπα*.

items.en: Let's leave it for tomorrow.
items.why: Nothing to fix: after *ας* the clitic goes before the verb: *ας το αφήσουμε*.

items.en: The book you lent me, I read in one day.

errs.why: When a definite object is put first for emphasis, a clitic repeats it before the verb: *το βιβλίο… το διάβασα*. This "clitic doubling" is obligatory.

items.en: I didn't see Giannis at all today.

errs.why: Same rule: a definite object moved to the front is doubled by a clitic: *τον Γιάννη δεν τον είδα*.

items.en: Looking at him carefully, I realised he was lying.

errs.why: With the gerund the clitic follows, as with the imperative: *κοιτάζοντάς τον*. The gerund then takes a second accent because its stress is on the third syllable from the end.

items.en: Just tell me!

errs.why: After an imperative, two clitics also go genitive first: *πες μου το*, *δώσ' του τα*.

items.en: I've told him a thousand times.

errs.why: In the perfect both clitics go before *έχω*, genitive first: *του το έχω πει*.

parts: Στη Μαρία της αρέσουν πολύ τα γλυκά.
items.en: Maria really likes sweets.
items.why: Nothing to fix: the person is named with *σε* and repeated by the clitic *της* (doubling), and *αρέσουν* agrees with *τα γλυκά*.

items.en: We have to do it today.

errs.why: Greek clitics do not move up to *πρέπει* or *μπορώ*: they stay with their own verb, after *να*: *πρέπει να το κάνουμε*.

items.en: Can you introduce him to me?

errs.why: Genitive before accusative: *να μου τον συστήσεις*.

items.en: Giving it to him, she told him to look after it.

errs.why: After a gerund both clitics follow, genitive first: *δίνοντάς του το*.

items.en: If you see him, tell him I'm looking for him.

errs.why: *αν* + subjunctive is not an imperative, so the clitic goes before the verb: *αν τον δεις*. Only the real imperative *πες* puts it after: *πες του*.

items.en: I'll never forget the things you told me.

errs.why: A fronted definite object, here the clause *αυτά που μου είπες*, is doubled by a clitic: *δεν θα τα ξεχάσω*.

items.en: Give them to them, so they calm down.
items.why: Nothing to fix: imperative + genitive *τους* + accusative *τα*; *δώσ'* is the usual elided *δώσε*.
